(a) No driver shall—

(1) Use alcohol, as defined in § 382.107 of this subchapter, or be under the influence of alcohol, within 4 hours before going on duty or operating, or having physical control of, a commercial motor vehicle; or

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately captures the prohibition against a driver using alcohol or being under the influence of alcohol within 4 hours before going on duty, operating, or having physical control of a commercial motor vehicle pursuant to paragraph (a)(1).

source_spans.quote: (a) No driver shall—

(2) Use alcohol, be under the influence of alcohol, or have any measured alcohol concentration or detected presence of alcohol, while on duty, or operating, or in physical control of a commercial motor vehicle; or

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately represents paragraph (a)(2), prohibiting drivers from using alcohol, being under the influence of alcohol, or having any measured alcohol concentration or detected presence of alcohol while on duty, operating, or in physical control of a commercial motor vehicle.

source_spans.quote: (a) No driver shall—

(3) Be on duty or operate a commercial motor vehicle while the driver possesses wine of not less than one-half of one per centum of alcohol by volume, beer as defined in 26 U.S.C. 5052(a), of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954, or distilled spirits as defined in section 5002(a)(8), of such Code. However, this does not apply to possession of wine, beer, or distilled spirits which are:

(i) Manifested and transported as part of a shipment; or

(ii) Possessed or used by bus passengers.

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately states the prohibition in paragraph (a)(3) barring a driver from being on duty or operating a commercial motor vehicle while possessing specified alcoholic beverages, including the referenced statutory definitions and exceptions.

source_spans.quote:
(b) No motor carrier shall require or permit a driver to—

(1) Violate any provision of paragraph (a) of this section; or

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim correctly reflects paragraph (b)(1), prohibiting a motor carrier from requiring or permitting a driver to violate any provision of paragraph (a).

source_spans.quote: (b) No motor carrier shall require or permit a driver to—

(2) Be on duty or operate a commercial motor vehicle if, by the driver's general appearance or conduct or by other substantiating evidence, the 
            
            driver appears to have used alcohol within the preceding four hours.

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately states paragraph (b)(2), prohibiting a motor carrier from requiring or permitting a driver to be on duty or operate a commercial motor vehicle if the driver appears to have used alcohol within the preceding four hours.

source_spans.quote: (c) Any driver who is found to be in violation of the provisons of paragraph (a) or (b) of this section shall be placed out-of-service immediately for a period of 24 hours.

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately conveys paragraph (c), requiring that any driver found in violation of paragraph (a) or (b) be placed out-of-service immediately for 24 hours.

source_spans.quote: (1) The 24-hour out-of-service period will commence upon issuance of an out-of-service order.

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim correctly reflects paragraph (c)(1), stating that the 24-hour out-of-service period commences upon issuance of an out-of-service order.

source_spans.quote: (2) No driver shall violate the terms of an out-of-service order issued under this section.

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately states paragraph (c)(2), prohibiting drivers from violating the terms of an out-of-service order issued under this section.

source_spans.quote:
(d) Any driver who is issued an out-of-service order under this section shall:

(1) Report such issuance to his/her employer within 24 hours; and

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim correctly captures paragraph (d)(1), requiring a driver issued an out-of-service order under this section to report its issuance to their employer within 24 hours.

source_spans.quote: (d) Any driver who is issued an out-of-service order under this section shall:

(2) Report such issuance to a State official, designated by the State which issued his/her driver's license, within 30 days unless the driver chooses to request a review of the order. In this case, the driver shall report the order to the State official within 30 days of an affirmation of the order by either the Division Administrator or State Director for the geographical area or the Administrator.

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately conveys paragraph (d)(2), including both the baseline 30-day reporting obligation to the designated State official and the alternative timing rule following affirmation upon administrative review.

source_spans.quote: (e) Any driver who is subject to an out-of-service order under this section may petition for review of that order by submitting a petition for review in writing within 10 days of the issuance of the order to the Division Administrator or State Director for the geographical area in which the order was issued. The Division Administrator or State Director may affirm or reverse the order. Any driver adversely affected by such order of the Regional Director of Motor Carriers may petition the Administrator for review in accordance with 49 CFR 386.13.

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately states the first sentence of paragraph (e), entitling a driver subject to an out-of-service order to petition for review in writing within 10 days of issuance to the Division Administrator or State Director.
